messages:
maria: Heads up — deploy-bot alerted on a small p95 spike in the eu1 smoke cohort after the 2.1.7 rollout. Not huge but consistent across 3 probes. Do we hold the next wave?

deploy-bot: Canary update for release/2.1.7 -> eu1: 12% traffic. Smoke probes: 3/20 failed, p95 420ms (baseline 260ms). Error surface: kv-cache-miss and transient 502s. Logs: short tail of rpc timeouts.

kev: I can see increased kvcache miss ratio on the eu1 hosts that received the new variant. Looks like prefix cache invalidation timing is off. Metric: kvcache_miss_rate -> +2.8pp at 12:34 UTC.

jordan: adding logs snippet from one host:
```
2026-03-19T12:34:21Z WARN kv_cache: miss key=prefix_xyz ttl=0 host=eu1-07
2026-03-19T12:34:21Z ERROR inference: rpc error: code=Unavailable desc=connect: connection reset
```

maria: Thanks. Is this a rollout-only thing or does it affect existing pinned traffic?

sam: Quick check — eu1 dedicated pool serving pinned 2.1.6 looks stable, no spike. This is confined to canary instances with 2.1.7 + quantization tweak.

kev: hypothesize: the version toggles a new kvcache invalidation window (config flag ttl_override=0) that wasn't enabled for all hosts; race causes fresh misses and backend pressure.

smoke-bot: Synthetic summary (last 10m):
- embed_smoke_probe: p95 410ms (baseline 240ms)
- kv_probe: 3 fails/20 (timeouts)
- http_5xx_rate: 0.9% -> up from 0.1%

maria: Proposed action: pause further waves, pin eu1 back to 2.1.6 (no full rollback global), open a tiny post-deploy note, and run a deeper kvcache trace on the canary hosts. Agree? @kev @jordan

kev: agree. I'll capture traces and try re-running with ttl_override off.

jordan: will collect host-level tcp/connect traces and heap profiles for the 2 canary hosts showing errors.

sam: I'll hold the next wave in deploybot and mark the release notes: "hold eu1 wave due to kvcache miss spike under new ttl flag". Also tagging infra oncall.

maria: If traces point to config drift, we can fast-follow with a config-only patch; if it's kernel/network related, we'll roll the canaries back.

deploy-bot: Action taken: paused rollout at 12:36 UTC. Traffic to 2.1.7 frozen. Pin action available: use `/deploy pin eu1 2.1.6`

kev: running trace now — attaching flamegraph link: https://grafana.company/internal/flame/abcd1234 (private)

jordan: noticed a burst of connection resets to kvcache proxy on the canary hosts around 12:33-12:35. Correlates with the p95 jump.

maria: OK let's pin eu1 and run a focused canary with ttl_override disabled. Sam, please execute pin. Kev/Jordan — let's target 15m trace window and then re-evaluate.

sam: Executing pin. `/deploy pin eu1 2.1.6 --reason "kvcache miss spike on 2.1.7 canary"`

deploy-bot: Pin executed: eu1 pinned to 2.1.6 at 12:40 UTC by sam. Canary instances serving 2.1.7 scaled down; traffic shifted back.

smoke-bot: Post-pin synthetic (5m):
- embed_smoke_probe p95 270ms
- kv_probe: 0/20 fails
- http_5xx_rate: 0.12%

maria: Good — metrics look back to baseline. Action items: 1) open a short post-deploy note in the release thread explaining the pin + traces, 2) flag for a config-only rollback candidate or a fix that disables ttl_override, 3) add a focused synthetic to the release gating to catch this earlier.

kev: I'll prep a config patch and run it in staging with the same synthetic before reattempt.

jordan: I'll add host tcp/connect alerts to make this class of failures more visible.

sam: I'll update the release notes and set the next wave on hold until we validate.

maria: Thanks everyone. Re-open this thread if post-pin metrics regress. For now, we keep eu1 pinned and follow up in the morning with a short RCA. :white_check_mark:
